# Hush, Baby  

This morning I longed once more to be just a little child,  
to have someone wrap me tight in an abba blanket, mild,  
carried close against her warm embrace, softly humming, free,  
where everything was right and whole and safe for me—  
at least those things I thought I knew,  
which turned out to be nothing, and surely still are too.  

So I wandered on a path,  
lost in thought, caught in a daze,  
or was it guilt? Regardless, I strayed—  
stumbling over dunes, gazing at the sea and mountains near,  
and there came a knowing; I’m wrapped in nature’s dear cloak here:  

Hush, hush, baby,  
hush now, softly, dear,  
Papa will come tomorrow,  
bringing sweet porridge near.
